amendment.decision: Context-aware native performance gates: ordinary responsiveness budgets unchanged; rebuild-window latency and rebuild-blocked rewards separately measured and bounded; macOS event-loop-lag p95 compared against its paired control when the runner baseline alone exceeds the absolute limit. 2026-09-21 (Wilson, Decision A): the same paired-control rule applies to event_loop_lag max_ms (max_control_delta_ms 50.0) — a lane passes when the runner baseline alone approaches the ceiling and addon-minus-control stays within the bound; the 200 ms ceiling itself is unchanged.

scoping_amendment.decision: endurance_memory retention (slope_mib_per_min / settled_increase_mib) on Qt 6.11 lanes is a tracked CI observation, not a release gate: evaluated as warnings via scope_endurance_failures() for nightly and release profiles only. Qt 6.5 and earlier keep failing; unparseable runtime info fails closed; the metric numbers themselves are unchanged in the payload and the scoping itself is recorded as a warning.
scoping_amendment.evidence: A2-a falsified the QtWebEngine flag pair as the cause (nightly 35692375494: flags OFF = macOS 39.5 MiB/min vs 4.0 with flags, Linux identical, no 0xC0000005 crash returned); local macOS with the same absent flags shows memory falling — the runner environment is the remaining differentiator.

reward_scoping_amendment.decision: An ordinary reward_completion p95 miss on a macOS runner is a documented warning, not a release gate: evaluated via scope_macos_reward_p95() for nightly and release profiles only, and only while p95 stays within 2x the limit (a gross regression keeps failing). The 250 ms limit is unchanged on every lane; Linux and Windows keep failing on a miss; the numbers stay in the payload and the scoping itself is recorded as a warning.
reward_scoping_amendment.evidence: release-verify 36330863967: macos-23.10 reward p95 245.6 / 254.8 / 253.7 across reps (aggregate 252.93), the same ~251-255 seen since nightly 36087409416, while all Linux/Windows lanes passed. Rewards have no paired control; the macOS runner alone costs ~148 ms event-loop lag p95 with no addon, against ~1-3 ms on Linux.

lag_max_amendment.decision: event_loop_lag max is judged on the median of each rep's worst ordinary sample instead of the single worst sample pooled across reps (max_verdict: median_rep_max), for both the 200 ms ceiling and the 50 ms paired-control delta; both thresholds are unchanged. A pooled single sample above max_backstop_ms (1000 ms) still fails on any lane, so a one-second freeze in any rep is never averaged away. The pooled max_ms, control_max_ms and every rep's max stay in the payload.
lag_max_amendment.evidence: Nightlies 2026-10-12..10-21 on unchanged code (aad24ed): 5 lane failures were budget:event_loop_lag:max with typical reps in budget (e.g. 38399323789 linux-23.10-qt6 addon reps 146.8/437.5/187.8 vs control 184.5/131.8/273.7; 39405375634 macos-23.10 233.6/170.0/198.9 vs 165.7/150.1/151.0). Replayed on those 5 plus all 7 lanes of green nightly 39020828590, the median rule passes all 12 (highest median 206.2 ms, macos-23.10, within 50 ms of its control); the largest pooled ordinary sample seen was 437.5 ms.

lag_max_scoping_amendment.decision: An event_loop_lag max miss (budget:event_loop_lag:max:median_rep:<x>, or the pooled fallback budget:event_loop_lag:max:<x>) on a macOS runner is a documented warning, not a release gate: evaluated via scope_macos_lag_max() for nightly and release profiles only, and only while the observed value the verdict used stays <= macos_max_scope_limit_ms (300.0, 1.5x the ceiling) AND the paired control is present with observed - control <= macos_max_scope_control_delta_ms (100.0). A missing control, max:backstop: failures, p95 lag failures and every Linux/Windows lane keep failing. The 200 ms ceiling and 50 ms control delta are unchanged on every lane; the numbers stay in the payload and the scoping itself is recorded as a warning.
lag_max_scoping_amendment.evidence: Nightly 39936385911 (2026-10-23), macos-23.10-qt6, native-performance failed only on budget:event_loop_lag:max:median_rep:200.478 (limit 200.0): addon rep maxima 177.897 / 200.535 / 200.478 (median 200.478) vs control rep maxima 149.072 / 145.775 / 173.061 (median 149.072), delta 51.4 vs 50.0. The macOS runner alone costs ~145-175 ms max lag with no addon (Linux/Windows controls ~8-25 ms), leaving the lane almost no headroom under 200 ms. Recent macOS medians: 164 vs 154 (10-22 mac-23), 192 vs 157 (10-22 mac-26), 206.2 (green run 39020828590 mac-23), 198.9 vs 151.0 (39405375634 mac-23).

note: Fixed acceptance targets from the AnkiScape reliability plan. These are not measured promises; changing one requires a documented plan amendment. Disk-full/locked-db failures are tested for safe degradation, not expected to meet normal successful-write latency.
